subject: social_science

concepts.title: Print Culture and Social Reform Debates
concepts.definition: The arrival of inexpensive printed materials like newspapers and tracts enabled public discussion on societal practices in regional vernaculars.
concepts.key_idea: Mass printing allowed common people to debate and participate in social reform.
question_patterns: how did print technology influence nineteenth century social reform debates
explain the role of newspapers and pamphlets in social movements
what made public discussions on social issues accessible to ordinary people
describe how printed literature helped spread reformist ideas
in what ways did modern communication transform social criticism

solution_steps.explain: Printed books and papers replaced expensive hand-copied manuscripts.
Vernacular publishing allowed common citizens to publish thoughts and join debates.

concepts.title: Abolition of Sati
concepts.definition: The eradication of the practice of burning widows on their deceased husbands pyres, accomplished through arguments rooted in ancient scriptures.
concepts.key_idea: Raja Rammohun Roy demonstrated that ancient texts did not support self-immolation of widows.
question_patterns: how did raja rammohun roy campaign against the practice of sati
when was sati legally banned in colonial india
what strategy did reformers use to prove sati lacked scriptural support
explain the role of British officials and Rammohun Roy in ending sati
describe the arguments used by advocates and opponents of sati

solution_steps.explain: Rammohun Roy showed Sanskrit texts lacked endorsement for widow burning.
Colonial authorities enacted a legal ban on sati in 1829.

concepts.title: Widow Remarriage Reform Movement
concepts.definition: Efforts by social reformers to secure legal approval and social acceptance for widows to marry again.
concepts.key_idea: Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar utilized ancient texts to support widow remarriage, leading to the law of 1856.
question_patterns: who was instrumental in passing the Hindu Widows Remarriage Act of 1856
how did Vidyasagar advocate for the rights of widows
which reform associations supported widow remarriage in different regions
what challenges did remarried widows face in society
explain the contribution of Veerasalingam Pantulu to widow reform

solution_steps.explain: Vidyasagar cited ancient scriptures permitting widows to marry again.

solution_steps.action: Note legal enactment and regional spread
solution_steps.explain: The 1856 Act was passed, and groups like Arya Samaj and Pantulus association championed the cause.

concepts.title: Promoting Female Education
concepts.definition: The establishment of formal educational institutions for young women despite traditional social fears and domestic restrictions.
concepts.key_idea: Reformers established schools for girls to improve womens position despite orthodox fears of social corruption.
question_patterns: why were people initially hesitant to send girls to formal schools
how did reformers like Vidyasagar and Phule promote female literacy
what methods did women like Rashsundari Debi use to educate themselves
explain how Muslim reformers advocated for girls education
which institutions provided curriculum for girls equal to boys

solution_steps.explain: Families feared public travel and neglected home duties.
Reformers built schools and women secretly learned reading at home.

concepts.title: Women Reformers and Feminist Literature
concepts.definition: Literary works and institutions created directly by women to critique patriarchal structures and promote female empowerment.
concepts.key_idea: Educated women authored critical texts and founded institutions to support womens independence.
question_patterns: what was the primary theme of Tarabai Shindes book Stripurushtulna
how did Pandita Ramabai support destitute and widowed women
describe the efforts of Begum Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain for girls education
what role did the Begums of Bhopal play in promoting education
how did women push for political rights like female suffrage in the early twentieth century

solution_steps.explain: Shinde exposed gender inequalities while Ramabai critiqued high-caste oppression.
Ramabai built widows shelters and Begum Rokeya founded schools in Patna and Calcutta.

concepts.title: Child Marriage Restraint Legislation
concepts.definition: Statutory provisions establishing minimum legal age thresholds for marriage to protect children from early marriage.
concepts.key_idea: The 1929 Act set legal minimum marriage ages for males and females to prevent child marriage.
question_patterns: calculate the age difference between male and female minimum legal marriage ages
what was the minimum age gap under the Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929
find the difference between male and female age limits in child marriage laws
determine how much older a male had to be than a female under the 1929 marriage law
compute the margin between minimum legal ages for men and women

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the female legal age limit from the male legal age limit.

concepts.title: Caste Reform and Social Mobility
concepts.definition: Efforts by reform societies and marginalized groups to challenge caste hierarchies and access new urban employment.
concepts.key_idea: Industrial growth and urban expansion offered low-caste individuals alternatives to traditional village servitude.
question_patterns: how did secret reform societies like Paramhans Mandali challenge caste taboos
what new job opportunities opened up for low-caste people during British rule
why did leatherworkers demand high prices during the First World War
how did migration to cities help low-caste labourers escape rural oppression
describe the role of Christian missionaries in educating low-caste children

solution_steps.explain: Secret societies violated caste food and touch taboos.
Factory jobs, municipal work, and overseas plantation labour offered alternative livelihoods.

concepts.title: Non-Brahman Equality Movements
concepts.definition: Social and spiritual movements organized within marginalized communities to promote self-respect and social parity.
concepts.key_idea: Non-Brahman leaders established regional movements to instil self-esteem and reject caste hierarchies.
question_patterns: who founded the Satnami movement and what was its objective
what was the main message of Shri Narayana Guru regarding caste
how did Haridas Thakurs Matua sect challenge Brahmanical authority
explain the slogan oru jati oru matam oru daivam manushyanu
how did grassroots caste movements seek to build self-esteem

solution_steps.explain: Ghasidas led Satnamis, Haridas worked in Bengal, Narayana Guru in Kerala.
Advocated human oneness and rejected caste-based discrimination.

concepts.title: Radical Caste Critiques Phule and Periyar
concepts.definition: Ideological attacks on Brahmanical supremacy proposing that indigenous populations were subjugated by non-native settlers.
concepts.key_idea: Phule and Periyar rejected elite claims to superiority and built movements for indigenous self-respect.
question_patterns: why did Jyotirao Phule dedicate his book Gulamgiri to American abolitionists
what arguments did Phule use against Aryan supremacy claims
explain the goals of the Satyashodhak Samaj founded by Phule
why did E V Ramaswamy Naicker Periyar launch the Self Respect Movement
how did Periyar critique classical religious scriptures like Manu and Ramayana

solution_steps.explain: Phule argued Aryans were outside conquerors who subjugated indigenous people.
Periyar advocated Dravidian self-respect and rejected orthodox religious texts enforcing inequality.

concepts.title: Temple Entry Movement and Dalit Assertion
concepts.definition: Sustained public campaigns organized by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to claim access to sacred spaces and public water sources for untouchables.
concepts.key_idea: Ambedkar led temple entry Satyagrahas to expose entrenched caste prejudice and assert human dignity.
question_patterns: what was the purpose of the temple entry movements led by Dr B R Ambedkar
how many temple entry movements did Ambedkar lead between 1927 and 1935
why were orthodox priests outraged during Ambedkars tank entry demonstration
what early childhood experiences shaped Ambedkars fight against caste
explain how temple entry satyagraha aimed to expose caste prejudice

solution_steps.explain: Ambedkar sought equal rights to public resources like temple water tanks.
Led three major campaigns from 1927 to 1935 demonstrating resistance to caste dominance.

concepts.title: Nineteenth-Century Reform Organizations
concepts.definition: Formal societies established across India to promote rational thought, education, and social reform while eliminating superstitious practices.
concepts.key_idea: Associations like Brahmo Samaj, Prarthana Samaj, and Aligarh Movement sought comprehensive social and religious renewal.
question_patterns: what were the key principles of the Brahmo Samaj
how did Derozio and Young Bengal movement promote radical thinking
explain the contribution of Sayyid Ahmed Khan and Aligarh Movement
what were the objectives of the Prarthana Samaj and Veda Samaj
how did the Singh Sabha movement reform Sikh practices

solution_steps.explain: Brahmo Samaj, Prarthana Samaj, Veda Samaj, and Aligarh Movement.
Opposed idolatry and caste, promoted female education, modern science, and scriptural reinterpretation.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Under the 1929 Act, the minimum legal age was {male_min_age} for men and {female_min_age} for women. Calculate the minimum age difference.

solution_template.explain: Subtract female minimum age from male minimum age.

worked_examples.question_pattern: When the minimum legal marriage age was revised to {male_min_age} for men and {female_min_age} for women, find the age difference.

solution_template.explain: Subtract female minimum age from male minimum age.

(c) Reformers received full support from all sections of society. (d) The Child Marriage Restraint Act was passed in 1829.
How did the knowledge of ancient texts help the reformers promote new laws?
What were the different reasons people had for not sending girls to school?
Why were Christian missionaries attacked by many people in the country? Why did some people support them?
In the British period, what new opportunities opened up for people from low castes?
How did Jyotirao Phule and other reformers justify their criticism of caste inequality in society?
Why did Phule dedicate his book Gulamgiri to the American movement to free slaves?
What did Ambedkar want to achieve through the temple entry movement?
Why were Jyotirao Phule and Ramaswamy Naicker critical of the national movement?
